The suite pins _PROJECT='REB' precisely so the configured-project branch is exercised, but the `or _DEFAULT_PROJECT` fallback (project_ensures.py:68) — a distinct behavior the docstring calls out — has no test. advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a swept ticketless store has NO committed .bridge_state/projects.json (seed returns ok, empty).
evidence: src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:114-115: `if not _store_has_tickets(tracker): return EnsureOutcome(SEED_ID, "ok", "no legacy tickets to migrate")`
docstring lines 110-113 describe the spurious-stamp risk this guard prevents
search `no legacy tickets` in tests returned (no matches); tests test_seed_* all call rebar.create_ticket before run_ensures
advisory.finding: The 'no legacy tickets to migrate' guard (project_ensures.py:114-115) has no asserting test. The contract — a fresh/empty store must NOT be seeded, so that adding a real second project later does not spuriously trip the multi-project stamp — is stated in the docstring but never verified: every test creates a ticket before sweeping, and no test asserts that an empty store still has NO committed projects.json after a sweep.
scenarios: A brand-new empty store is swept; a regression that drops the ticketless guard would pre-populate the project set and later trip the multi-project stamp spuriously

advisory.finding: No test verifies the stamp preserves pre-existing compat keys. The stamp unit's central documented design (it does NOT call compat.write_compat_record, which resets required_capabilities to [], and it preserves every other key such as epoch) is untested: test_multi_project_store_is_stamped only asserts the token is present in required_capabilities, never that a prior key like `epoch` survives the stamp. A regression switching to write_compat_record or overwriting the record would still pass.
scenarios: A stamped store had a pre-existing epoch (or other compat key); a regression using write_compat_record or full overwrite drops it

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Check the `git commit` (and `git add`) returncode in seed_projects_mapping_unit / converge_multi_project_stamp_unit and return "failed" (or ensure branch identity) when the commit does not land.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:127: `_git(tracker, "add", _PROJECTS_REL_PATH)`
src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:128-135 commit call whose CompletedProcess.returncode is discarded
`return EnsureOutcome(SEED_ID, "changed", ...)` returned unconditionally after the commit

Unlike init._gitignore_unit which also ignores the return code, these units run at MCP boot / fsck --repair on legacy stores where _ensure_branch_user_config (init.py:457) is not guaranteed to have run in the same invocation, so a missing tickets-branch identity makes the commit fail silently
dropped.finding: Neither seed_projects_mapping_unit nor converge_multi_project_stamp_unit checks the returncode of its `git commit`; if the commit fails (e.g. missing branch user.name/user.email, a rejecting hook despite --no-verify, or nothing staged), the unit still returns EnsureOutcome status "changed" and run_ensures records the id as applied, yet nothing was committed. On the next sweep the `git show tickets:...` check (seed) fails again → rewrite/re-add/re-commit-fail loops silently, and the stamp's fail-closed guarantee is not actually persisted.
dropped.suggested_fix: Capture the CompletedProcess from the commit; if returncode != 0, return EnsureOutcome(<id>, "failed", commit.stderr) so the marker excludes it and the next sweep retries, rather than reporting "changed".

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _effective_project() tolerate ConfigError (fall back to os.environ JIRA_PROJECT or DIG) to match Backend.project's documented degrade-not-break behavior.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:66-68: `from rebar.config import load_config` then `return load_config().jira.project or _DEFAULT_PROJECT`

acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:126-129) catches ConfigError and falls back to os.environ JIRA_PROJECT — the docstring at project_ensures.py:60-65 claims equivalence to Backend.project but does not replicate this fallback
dropped.finding: _effective_project() calls load_config().jira.project with no exception handling, so a ConfigError propagates and records projects-seed as "failed", whereas the mirrored Backend.project (via resolve_jira_settings) degrades to env-only on ConfigError. On a store with a transiently-unparseable rebar.toml the seed never converges.
